svg.title: Keep all pairwise comparisons in one family
svg.desc: Tukey controls the chance of one or more false positives in the comparison family at five percent under the classical assumptions. A Tukey-adjusted p-value can be compared directly with 0.05.
svg.text: Three groups give three pairwise comparisons
Running separate unadjusted tests raises the chance of a false positive.
Tukey controls the familywise error rate at 5%
Use the adjusted p-value or read the simultaneous 95% interval.
The plot shows the signed gap and its interval.
An interval entirely above or below zero gives adjusted p < 0.05.
Classical HSD assumes independent observations, normal errors and equal variances.
For unequal group sizes, Tukey–Kramer uses a cutoff for each pair.
